items.text:
अनृतं साहसं माया मूर्खत्वम् अतिलोभिता ।
अशौचत्वं निर्दयत्वं स्त्रीणां दोषाः स्वभावजाः ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
anṛtaṃ sāhasaṃ māyā mūrkhatvam atilobhitā |
aśaucatvaṃ nirdayatvaṃ strīṇāṃ doṣāḥ svabhāvajāḥ || 1 ||
items.en: Lying, rashness, trickery, foolishness, too much greed, uncleanliness and cruelty are faults said to be natural in women.

items.text:
भोज्यं भोजनशक्तिश्च रतिशक्तिर्वराड्गना ।
विभवो दानशक्तिश्च नाऽल्पस्य तपसः फलम् ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
bhojyaṃ bhojanaśaktiśca ratiśaktirvarāḍganā |
vibhavo dānaśaktiśca nā'lpasya tapasaḥ phalam || 2 ||
items.en: Having good food and the power to digest it, desire and a lovely wife, wealth and the will to give it: these come only from great past merit.

items.text:
यस्य पुत्रो वशीभूतो भार्या छन्दानुगामिनी ।
विभवे यश्च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य स्वर्ग इहैव हि ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
yasya putro vaśībhūto bhāryā chandānugāminī |
vibhave yaśca santuṣṭastasya svarga ihaiva hi || 3 ||
items.en: One whose son obeys him, whose wife follows his wishes, and who is content with what he has, finds heaven here on earth.

items.text:
ते पुत्रा ये पितुर्भक्ताः स पिता यस्तु पोषकः ।
तन्मित्रंयत्रविश्वासःसा भार्या यत्र निवृतिः ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
te putrā ye piturbhaktāḥ sa pitā yastu poṣakaḥ |
tanmitraṃyatraviśvāsaḥsā bhāryā yatra nivṛtiḥ || 4 ||
items.en: True sons are those devoted to their father; a true father is one who cares for them; a true friend is one you can trust; a true wife is one who brings peace.

items.text:
परोक्षे कार्य्यहन्तारं प्रत्यक्षे प्रियवादिनम्॥
वर्ज्जयेत्तादृशं मित्रं विषकुम्भम्पयोमुखम् ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
parokṣe kāryyahantāraṃ pratyakṣe priyavādinam||
varjjayettādṛśaṃ mitraṃ viṣakumbhampayomukham || 5 ||
items.en: Avoid a friend who ruins your work behind your back and speaks sweetly to your face; he is like a pot of poison with milk on top.

items.text:
न विश्वसेत्कुमित्रे च मित्रे चापि न विश्वसेत् ।
कदाचित्कुपितं मित्रं सर्वगुह्यं प्रकाशयेत् ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
na viśvasetkumitre ca mitre cāpi na viśvaset |
kadācitkupitaṃ mitraṃ sarvaguhyaṃ prakāśayet || 6 ||
items.en: Do not trust a bad friend, and do not fully trust even a good friend; if he becomes angry one day, he may tell all your secrets.

items.text:
मनसा चिन्तितं कार्यं वचसा न प्रकाशयेत् ।
मंत्रेण रक्षयेद् गूढं कार्य्य चापि नियोजयेत् ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
manasā cintitaṃ kāryaṃ vacasā na prakāśayet |
maṃtreṇa rakṣayed gūḍhaṃ kāryya cāpi niyojayet || 7 ||
items.en: Do not speak out a plan you have made in your mind; guard it closely like a secret and carry it out in action.

items.text:
कष्टञ्च खलु मूर्खत्वं कष्टं च खलु यौवनम् ।
कष्टात् कष्टतरं चैव परगेहे निवासनम् ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
kaṣṭañca khalu mūrkhatvaṃ kaṣṭaṃ ca khalu yauvanam |
kaṣṭāt kaṣṭataraṃ caiva paragehe nivāsanam || 8 ||
items.en: Foolishness is painful, and youth is painful too, but living in another person's house is the most painful of all.

items.text:
शैले शैले न माणिक्यं मौक्तिकं न गजे गजे ।
साधवो नहि सर्वत्र चन्दनं न वने वने ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
śaile śaile na māṇikyaṃ mauktikaṃ na gaje gaje |
sādhavo nahi sarvatra candanaṃ na vane vane || 9 ||
items.en: Not every mountain has rubies, not every elephant has a pearl, not every forest has sandalwood, and good people are not found everywhere.

items.text:
पुत्राश्च विविधैः शीलैर्नियोज्याः सततं बुधैः ।
नीतिज्ञाः शीलसम्पन्ना भवन्ति कुलपूजिताः ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
putrāśca vividhaiḥ śīlairniyojyāḥ satataṃ budhaiḥ |
nītijñāḥ śīlasampannā bhavanti kulapūjitāḥ || 10 ||
items.en: Wise parents should always train their sons in good conduct; sons who know right ways and have good character are honoured by the family.

items.text:
माता शत्रुः पिता वैरी येन बालो न पाठितः ।
न शोभते सभामध्ये हंसमध्ये वको यथा ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
mātā śatruḥ pitā vairī yena bālo na pāṭhitaḥ |
na śobhate sabhāmadhye haṃsamadhye vako yathā || 11 ||
items.en: A mother and father who do not educate their child are its enemies; such a child looks out of place in an assembly, like a crane among swans.

items.text:
लालनाद् बहवो दोषास्ताडनाद् बहवो गुणाः ।
तस्मात्पुत्रं च शिष्यं च ताडयेन्नतुलालयेत् ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
lālanād bahavo doṣāstāḍanād bahavo guṇāḥ |
tasmātputraṃ ca śiṣyaṃ ca tāḍayennatulālayet || 12 ||
items.en: Spoiling brings many faults and discipline brings many virtues; so discipline a son or a pupil, and do not spoil him.

items.text:
श्लोकेन वा तदर्ध्दाऽर्ध्दाक्षरेण वा ।
अवन्घ्यं दिवसं कुर्याद्दानाध्ययनकर्मभिः ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
ślokena vā tadardhdā'rdhdākṣareṇa vā |
avanghyaṃ divasaṃ kuryāddānādhyayanakarmabhiḥ || 13 ||
items.en: Make each day useful by learning a verse, half a verse, a quarter, or even one letter, and by giving and good deeds.

items.text:
कान्ता वियोगः स्वजनापमानि ।
रणस्य शेषः कुनृपस्य सेवा ॥
दरिद्रभावो विषमा सभा च ।
विनाग्निना ते प्रदहन्ति कायम् ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
kāntā viyogaḥ svajanāpamāni |
raṇasya śeṣaḥ kunṛpasya sevā ||
daridrabhāvo viṣamā sabhā ca |
vināgninā te pradahanti kāyam || 14 ||
items.en: Separation from a loved wife, insults from one's own people, an unpaid debt, serving a bad king, poverty, and an unfair assembly burn the body without fire.

items.text:
नदीतीरे च ये वृक्षाः परगेहेषु कामिनी ।
मंत्रिहीनाश्च राजानः शीघ्रं नश्यन्त्यसंशयम् ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
nadītīre ca ye vṛkṣāḥ parageheṣu kāminī |
maṃtrihīnāśca rājānaḥ śīghraṃ naśyantyasaṃśayam || 15 ||
items.en: Trees on a river bank, a woman who lives in other men's houses, and kings without good advisers all perish quickly, without doubt.

items.text:
बलं विद्या च विप्राणां राज्ञां सैन्यं बलं तथा ।
बलंवित्तञ्चवैश्यानां शूद्राणां परिचर्यिका ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
balaṃ vidyā ca viprāṇāṃ rājñāṃ sainyaṃ balaṃ tathā |
balaṃvittañcavaiśyānāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ paricaryikā || 16 ||
items.en: The strength of priests is learning, the strength of kings is their army, the strength of traders is wealth, and the strength of workers is service.

items.text:
निर्धनं पुरुषं वेश्या प्रजा भग्नं नृपं त्यजेत् ।
खगा वीतफलं वृक्षं भुक्त्वा चाभ्यागतो गृहम् ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
nirdhanaṃ puruṣaṃ veśyā prajā bhagnaṃ nṛpaṃ tyajet |
khagā vītaphalaṃ vṛkṣaṃ bhuktvā cābhyāgato gṛham || 17 ||
items.en: A prostitute leaves a man who has no money, subjects leave a defeated king, birds leave a tree with no fruit, and a guest leaves a house after eating.

items.text:
गृहीत्वा दक्षिणां विप्रास्त्यजन्ति यजमानकम् ।
प्राप्तविद्यागुरुंशिष्योदग्धारण्यंमृगास्तथा ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
gṛhītvā dakṣiṇāṃ viprāstyajanti yajamānakam |
prāptavidyāguruṃśiṣyodagdhāraṇyaṃmṛgāstathā || 18 ||
items.en: Priests leave the patron once paid, a pupil leaves the teacher once he has learned, and deer leave a forest once it has burned.

items.text:
दुराचारी दुरादृष्टिर्दुरावासी च दुर्जनः ।
यन्मैत्रीक्रियते पुम्भिर्नरःशीघ्रं विनश्यति ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr:
durācārī durādṛṣṭirdurāvāsī ca durjanaḥ |
yanmaitrīkriyate pumbhirnaraḥśīghraṃ vinaśyati || 19 ||
items.en: A man who makes friends with someone of bad conduct, evil eyes, a bad place of living, or a wicked nature is soon ruined.

items.text:
समाने शोभते प्रीतिः राज्ञि सेवा च शोभते ।
वाणिज्यं व्यवहारेषु स्त्री दिव्या शोभते गृहे ॥ २० ॥
items.tr:
samāne śobhate prītiḥ rājñi sevā ca śobhate |
vāṇijyaṃ vyavahāreṣu strī divyā śobhate gṛhe || 20 ||
items.en: Friendship looks good between equals, service looks good under a king, trade looks good in business, and a good woman looks good in the home.
